inline_comments.comment: The new example uses ` ```mermaid ` as the code fence language, but every other interactive example in this source file (102 occurrences) uses ` ```mermaid-example `. As confirmed in `packages/mermaid/scripts/docs.mts` (line 71), `MERMAID_EXAMPLE_KEYWORDS` includes both `mermaid` and `mermaid-example`, so they produce identical build output. However, consistency with the existing convention means this should be ` ```mermaid-example `.

"E.g." at the very end of a sentence, immediately before a standalone code block, is awkward. "E.g." (Latin: *exempli gratia*) is conventionally used inline before a short parenthetical example, not as the last word of a closing sentence. Consider ending with a colon instead: "...to constrain the aspect ratio:" or rephrasing to "For example:"

The new paragraph tells users to set `h` and `constraint: on`, but doesn't explicitly warn against also setting `w`. The PR description says 'Setting the width (w) instead causes inconsistent rendering', yet that caution is absent from the docs. Consider adding a note such as: "Do not set `w` when `constraint: on` is used, as this leads to inconsistent rendering."

This file's own header (line 3) explicitly states "THIS IS AN AUTOGENERATED FILE. DO NOT EDIT." and instructs edits to go to the source file in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`. Directly committing changes to `docs/syntax/flowchart.md` bypasses that contract. The correct workflow is to edit only the source file and then run `pnpm --filter mermaid run docs:build` (or `pnpm --filter mermaid run docs:build --git`) to regenerate this file. In this PR the content happens to match what the build would produce, but landing manual edits to an autogenerated file makes the repo fragile: the next docs build will overwrite any untracked differences, and future reviewers cannot rely on the generated file being authoritative.

general_comments.comment: The general image-shape syntax example near the top of the section (unchanged by this PR) shows `w: 60, h: 60, constraint: "off"`. After this PR, users who see that example may attempt the analogous `w: 60, h: 60, constraint: "on"` — precisely the combination the PR description identifies as causing inconsistent rendering. A brief clarifying note on the `w` parameter (e.g. "Avoid combining `w` with `constraint: \"on\"`") would close that documentation gap.
